document.outcome: Photoelectric equation; work function; maximum kinetic energy

content.text: Light of wavelength 310 nm is incident on a clean metal surface in a vacuum. The work function of the metal is 2.9 eV.
What is the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted from the surface?
Thinks the work function is the energy the electron receives
Does not subtract the work function; takes the whole photon energy as kinetic energy: 4.0 eV
Adds the work function instead of subtracting it: 4.0 + 2.9 = 6.9 eV

content.text: An alpha particle and a proton have the same kinetic energy. Both move at speeds much less than the speed of light. The mass of the alpha particle is four times the mass of the proton.
What is the ratio (de Broglie wavelength of the alpha particle) / (de Broglie wavelength of the proton)?
Takes λ ∝ 1/m (assumes the speeds are equal): 1/4
Thinks particles with equal kinetic energy have equal wavelengths (applies a relation valid for photons to matter)
). λ = h / p ∝ 1 / √m (for the same E
A photon of wavelength 3.00 pm is scattered by an electron that is initially at rest. The photon is scattered through an angle of 180°. The change in wavelength of a photon scattered through an angle
What is the wavelength of the scattered photon?
Takes cos 180° = +1; the shift comes out as zero
Takes the wavelength shift to be the wavelength of the scattered photon: 4.86 pm
Takes the factor (1 − cos θ) as 1 (the value for 90°): 3.00 + 2.43 = 5.43 pm
Δλ = 2.43 × (1 − cos 180°) = 2.43 × 2 = 4.86 pm. The wavelength of the scattered photon = 3.00 + 4.86 = 7.86 pm.

document.outcome: Photoelectric observation not explained by the wave model; threshold frequency

content.text: Monochromatic light is incident on a metal surface and the emission of photoelectrons is investigated.
be explained by the wave model of light?
The photoelectric current is proportional to the intensity of the light.
Thinks every prediction of the photon model contradicts the wave model; more electrons being emitted as intensity increases is also consistent with the wave model
Energy is transferred from the light to electrons in the metal.
Thinks energy transfer is specific to the particle model; waves also carry energy
No electrons are emitted below a certain frequency, however intense the light.
The emitted electrons have a range of kinetic energies.
Thinks a range of kinetic energies is evidence for photons; electrons being at different depths and binding energies in the metal gives a range in both models

In the wave model energy is transferred continuously; light that is intense enough (or lasts long enough) should be able to release electrons whatever its frequency. A threshold frequency independent of intensity can only be explained by photons of energy hf.

document.outcome: Particle diffraction; de Broglie wavelength; wave–particle duality

content.text: Electrons are accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 150 V in a vacuum tube. The electron beam passes through a thin film of graphite and then strikes a fluorescent screen. A pattern of bright concentric rings is seen on the screen.

stimuli.description: Evacuated glass tube. Electron gun on the left (150 V between cathode and anode), a thin graphite film in the middle, a fluorescent screen on the right. On the screen, concentric bright rings around the central bright spot. Diagram not to scale.

content.text: Show that the de Broglie wavelength of the electrons is about 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
Answer must be given to at least 3 s.f. (1.00 × 10⁻¹⁰) from a visible substitution for MP3.
Outline how the pattern on the screen provides evidence for the wave nature of electrons.
the rings are a diffraction / interference pattern
diffraction / interference is a property of waves
particles alone would give a single spot / no rings
Accept reference to the spacing of atoms in graphite being comparable to the wavelength for MP2.
The accelerating potential difference is increased.
Predict, with a reason, the change in the diameters of the rings.
diffraction angles are smaller so the diameters decrease
MP2 requires the direction of the change in diameter.
Calculate, in eV, the energy of a photon that has the same wavelength as the electrons in (a).
